paragraphs: On Thursday evening, Lily sat at the table with her laptop. She wanted to see the weather forecast for the weekend. Tom looked at the screen over her shoulder. The forecast had three days. Each day had a small picture. Mia came from next door and sat next to Lily. "Let's read it together," said Mia.

First, Lily read the forecast for Friday and Saturday. "Friday: sunny and hot, thirty-three degrees." The picture showed a big yellow sun. "Saturday: cloudy in the morning, and sunny in the afternoon, thirty degrees." The picture showed a sun behind a small gray cloud. "Saturday morning is perfect for a walk," said Mia. "It will not be too hot, and we can see butterflies in the park."

Then Lily read the forecast for Sunday. "Sunday: a thunderstorm in the afternoon, twenty-eight degrees." The picture showed a dark cloud with rain. "There will probably be a big storm after lunch," said Tom. "Perhaps it will start at two o'clock." Leo called Lily on the phone. He was mad. "I wanted to play football in the park on Sunday afternoon!" he said. "We can play in the morning," said Lily.

Next, the children made a short plan. "On Saturday morning, Mia and I will walk to the park," said Lily. "Tom will come with us, and he will take his camera." "On Sunday morning, Leo will play football with us before the storm." "If it rains before eleven o'clock, we will stay at home." "We will play a board game instead." Mia wrote the plan on a sheet of paper. She put it on the fridge.

On Friday evening, Lily packed her backpack for Saturday. She put in a bottle of water and a hat. She added an extra bottle for Mia, because Mia often forgot her water. She also put in a small raincoat, because the weather can change. Mom looked at the backpack. "Do you need anything else, Lily?" she asked. "No, Mom, the raincoat is enough, so I do not need an umbrella," said Lily.
